results.title: ZooWork: The AI agent delivery platform for FDEs and domain experts | Product Hunt
results.content:
Justin Jincaid

I love the product concept.

Imagine a founder could build an agent that drafts investor updates from approved company notes, then share it with teammates for review, that will be very helpful.

David Lu

@justin2025 The approved notes are what make this work, since an update is only as good as what the founder has already signed off on. You'd load those notes into the Agent's knowledge base, write the update format and tone into its job description, and set it to run on a monthly schedule. The draft then goes to your teammates through a share link or Slack, and they review it before anything reaches investors. The knowledge base is free on ZooWork for a limited time, so it's a good moment to try it with last month's notes and see whether the draft sticks to them. [...] ZooWork

What do you think? …

Justin Jincaid

I love the product concept. [...] Since then, we've heard one thing over and over, and felt it ourselves: there are countless tools for building AI agents, but almost nothing for delivering them. Everyone has an agent that works beautifully on their laptop. Almost no one can hand it to a client, a team, or a paying user as a reliable service.

That gap changed what we build, and our name along with it. ZooWork is our answer: an agent delivery platform for forward-deployed engineers, developers, and domain experts, with the whole path from build to production in one place.

Build: Describe what you want in the no-code Builder, or stay in the coding agent you already use (Claude Code, Codex, and more) and ship through our Managed Agent API. Setup is one line:

`npx skills add SerendipityOneInc/zoowork-sdk-skills`

Hi Product Hunt! I'm Ning, founder of ZooClaw.

Back in February, I was playing around with OpenClaw and built an AI companion agent — just for fun. I shared it with my team.

What happened next really surprised me.

My HR lead — zero technical background — started playing with it and somehow turned her own expertise into a career planning agent. 33 iterations in one afternoon. It's now live on ZooClaw for anyone to use.

Another colleague built a social media agent. A post it created went viral overnight.

People didn't just use the agent — with the right tool, they started creating their own. [...] Report

Ning Hu

ZooWork

@artem\_kosilov Both! We just got started, but even from our very limited early user study, we've been amazed at how much people are willing to interact with and trust the specialist agents — and how easy it is for non-techies to build their own. We see a productivity boom coming from both sides, and honestly we're just excited to see where users take it.

Report

@ninghu Really interesting approach with proactive agents — especially the idea of routing tasks across models.

I’ve been working on data pipelines and was thinking about how you might track agent performance and outputs across different models.

Curious — are you already building internal analytics for that, or is it something you're planning?

@laura\_yang1 Thank you for the kind words and the thoughtful question! Privacy and reliability are absolutely top of mind for us. We're currently in the process of obtaining SOC 2 Type 1 and GDPR compliance, both coming very soon. Error prevention and reliability safeguards for critical workflows are also on our roadmap. We're building ZooClaw to be something teams can genuinely trust — thanks for pushing us on this!
